root_idea.summary: The root develops along two principal lines: alternating or circulating something between parties, and impairment or absence of sight in one eye.
root_idea.development: From the eye-related line, the lexicon extends to what is exposed, vulnerable, defective, or requiring concealment; from the alternating line come reciprocal action, lending, and related transferred uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun is presented under the normalized singular citation form عَوْرَة.

senses.definition: A private part or other aspect of a person that is normally concealed because exposing it is shameful or improper.
senses.usage_conditions: In 24:31, the plural refers to the private parts or concealed aspects of women; the term may also denote anything whose exposure is considered shameful.

senses.definition: A time of privacy, when private parts or household privacy may be exposed.
senses.usage_conditions: In 24:58, the plural denotes the three customary periods of privacy: before dawn prayer, at midday, and after the night prayer.

senses.definition: A vulnerable, exposed, or undefended condition; specifically, a house or dwelling that is open to danger or attack.
senses.usage_conditions: In 33:13, عَوْرَةٌ is used predicatively of houses claimed to be exposed or defenceless, rather than referring to bodily private parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become blind in one eye; of an eye, to become blind, sunken, or dried up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or to the affected eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a well, to become filled up or spoiled so that its water dries up; to block or fill the well and stop its springs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use for wells and water sources.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone one-eyed; to put out an eye or make it sink in its socket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person or the eye itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a person or thing away; hence, to destroy or cause it to perish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is reported especially in negative expressions and proverbial usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take, do, strike, or affect something by turns; to alternate or reciprocally exchange an action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people sharing an action, of successive blows, and of things acting upon one another in succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To measure or calibrate measures.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction referring to vessels or measures.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lend a thing or give someone the use of it without an exchange; a loan or borrowed use.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The thing itself is ordinarily returned when it remains available; the reciprocal form can describe lending between parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To appear or become within a person's power or reach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used, for example, of game that has come within reach of the hunter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have an exposed or vulnerable opening or spot, such as a place liable to striking, piercing, or breach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, a building, or another structure with an exposed weak point.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask for, seek, or obtain a loan; to borrow a thing for use.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may retain مِنْ before the lender or omit the preposition; it can also take the borrowed object directly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise and transfer an arrow from its quiver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative or extended use of transferring an object from one place to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The metaphorical transfer or use of a word or expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes metaphorical usage rather than a literal loan.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fault, defect, imperfection, blemish, or unsoundness; in an article, garment, structure, or animal, a hole, rent, burn, or rottenness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact manifestation varies with the damaged object; the core meaning is a defect or condition making it unsound or blemished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unguarded or exposed place or route where attack, loss, being cut off, or other danger is feared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a place without a keeper or protection and of a route containing a dangerous opening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman or women, by extension from something whose appearance is regarded as shameful or requiring concealment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or assumed-tropical application, not the basic anatomical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of concealment or a hiding place suitable for covering or protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-based extension of the notion of what must be concealed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gap, opening, or breach in a frontier, hostile country, or battle line through which slaughter or attack may be feared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a strategic vulnerability in a boundary or military position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cleft or fissure in a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may denote mountain clefts or fissures collectively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well in a state of demolition or ruin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Here the otherwise plural-looking form is used as a singular description of a ruined well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An eye ailment, especially ophthalmia, irritating fluid, thick matter, or a mote in the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also denote small pustules or matter affecting the eyelid; it is a noun rather than an active participle in this usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quantity of wealth so great that it fills, overwhelms, or confounds the sight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually said of abundant camels or comparable property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow or stone whose source or shooter is unknown; by extension, scattered arrows or a scattered swarm of locusts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression emphasizes uncertain origin or scattered movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One-eyed, blind in one eye, or squint-eyed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people and animals; the feminine is عَوْرَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained either through an inauspicious association or ironically through the bird's sharp sight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert in which there is no water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional epithet for a waterless desert.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road in which there is no sign by which to find the way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of a route lacking guidance or visible markers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A night, morning, or year in which there is no cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional weather-related epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad, corrupt, abominable, or disapproved in a thing, disposition, temperament, or nature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended evaluative use of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bad substitute or an inferior successor replacing someone or something better.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional proverbial expression applied to a disparaged replacement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A foul, abominable, or irrational word, saying, or action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to speech or conduct that departs from reason, rectitude, or what the hearer accepts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Obscure, subtle, or difficult-to-grasp meanings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural application of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A worse successor following a better one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of the noun; the lexical explanation is preserved as an attributed alternative alongside the eye-related interpretation.

cautions: The Quranic noun has distinct privacy and vulnerability uses: 24:31 and 24:58 concern concealed private matters or times of privacy, while 33:13 describes houses as exposed or undefended.
